newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND WRAP UP AUSTRALIAN INNINGS BUT LOSE ATHERTON.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND WRAP UP AUSTRALIAN INNINGS BUT LOSE ATHERTON.

text.p: England quickly wrapped up the Australian first innings for 235 but then lost their captain Michael Atherton cheaply on the second day of the third test at Old Trafford on Friday.
Atherton, batting on his home ground, touched a delivery from Glenn McGrath to wicket-keeper Ian Healy after making only five.
Although conditions were not as difficult as on the first day, with the pitch less green and drying out in the morning sun, England made slow progress and at lunch were 37 for one off 18 overs.
Leg-spinner Shane Warne, who made his name at Old Trafford on the 1993 tour, was brought on early and encouraged his team by immediately troubling opener Mark Butcher.

Shortly afterwards Warne might have run Butcher out but narrowly missed with an under-arm throw from close-range as the batsman struggled to make his ground. Butcher was 17 not out at the interval, with his Surrey team mate Alec Stewart on 13.
Earlier, England needed less than 40 minutes to finish off the Australian innings, taking the remaining three wickets for 11 runs in 8.3 overs.
Paul Reiffel was yorked by Darren Gough for 31, having provided invaluable support for Steve Waugh in an eighth-wicket stand of 70.

Gough then removed Waugh's middle stump via his bat and pad. The Australian vice-captain had made 108 off 175 balls and received generous applause from the England team as well as another capacity crowd.

Dean Headley had Jason Gillespie caught behind for a duck, wicket-keeper Stewart equalling the Ashes record of six catches in an innings held by fellow countryman Jack Russell and Australians Rodney Marsh and Ian Healy.
Headley, in an impressive test debut, finished the innings with figures of four for 72.
